chapter: Fish fries, passing the hat and district living
title: Gold from Norwegian sailors, diamonds, and women hustling for him
summary: Dawson recalls Norwegian ships' gold coins, wearing diamond studs and cufflinks made of ten-dollar gold pieces, and living off women's earnings and his gambling.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, you see we had them time. We had them Norwegian ships used to come down. And them Norwegians used to come in, you know, loaded down with money, gold money. You could carry gold money at that time, gold money. They'd have ten dollar gold piece mixed up with pennies and you couldn't hardly tell the difference because it was hard to tell the difference between a ten dollar gold piece and a dime, a silver dime. It was small, you see. And many times we used to be whacking up the money after we'd get through playing. And Mary Minetta said, that's a ten dollar gold piece then, man. That ain't no ten copper cent. You see, that's a ten dollar. I had a cuff button. I had a cuff links made out of ten dollar gold pieces. A whole set. Because I was sporting when I was young, when I was playing, man. I used to have diamond studs, just all that. I used to dress all up, you know.
What did you dress up like that for?
I was sweet, round the district. I had women hustling for me.
Would they give you the diamonds? Would they give me money? Did they give you diamonds?

They give me, what I would take to get it, sure. I'd get money, buy diamonds, buy what I wore. Buy anything I wore. Me and Mary Minetta, me and him was like that. And I used to gamble too, you see. I was tough round there. I'd get with them guys, you know. We'd gamble round there. And I used to make some good hauls, you see. I was there, you know. I wasn't married then. I was single. But I'd make a good night. I'd catch a good night. I'd catch a good night. Need for a hundred, two hundred dollars. I'd go right down back to Barber Street there and I'd go back in my room back there. I'd stay with my mama, you know. I'd go back there, I had a little suitcase. They'd run it down there under the bed. They'd stay there, nobody wouldn't bother.
